Where it began

Temba Bavuma was born in Cape Town on 17 May 1990 and grew up in Langa, a suburb where cricket is taken very seriously. It must have been a good street to play on: Thami Tsolekile and Malusi Siboto, who also went on to play first-class cricket, came from the same one.

His schooling began in Newlands, at South African College Junior School, and finished at St David's Marist Inanda, a boys' school in Sandton. He made his first-class debut for Gauteng in 2008 and became a heavy scorer for the Lions, with 637 runs in the 2011-12 season and 714 two seasons later.

The player

A right-handed batter, he first played Test cricket on Boxing Day 2014, against the West Indies. At Cape Town in January 2016 he made 102 not out against England, becoming the first black African to score a Test hundred for South Africa. Later that year he made a hundred on his one-day debut, against Ireland.

By November 2026 he had played 68 Tests, making 3,993 runs at 38.77 with five hundreds and 26 fifties. His best, 179 against Australia at Gqeberha in October 2026, was the fourth-highest by any South Africa captain in a Test at home.

The captain

In 2021 he became South Africa's first black African permanent captain, taking charge of the one-day side, and later he was given the Test team too. He led them to the 2023-25 World Test Championship title. In November 2025 his side went to India and won both Tests, the second by 408 runs, for South Africa's first series win there in 25 years. His unbeaten 55 in the first Test was the only fifty of the match.

By November 2026 he had captained South Africa in 13 Tests and won 11 of them, losing only one.

What made him special

He was at his best when a series was in the balance. When India toured in 2021-22 he made 221 runs at 73.66 as South Africa won 2-1. If he could have asked for one thing more, it might have been for a few more of his 26 Test fifties to become hundreds, a knack he had shown plenty of for the Lions.

He bowled a little, too. His first Test wicket came against Australia in November 2016, and ten years later it had yet to be joined by a second. One, he might say, is enough to prove the point.

And finally

His first ODI hundred came while he was standing in as an opener for Hashim Amla. Not many players are handed a borrowed spot at the top of the order on debut and give it back with a century and a player of the match award.
